plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: Towering stalks carry huge golden flower heads that turn to follow the sun. Their dark centers are ringed with bright yellow petals. Whole fields glow like a sea of suns.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early autumn (roughly July to September in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Central and Northern Europe, and the Great Plains of North America
plants.funFact: A sunflower head is made up of hundreds to thousands of tiny individual flowers, called florets. Each floret can become a seed. The spiral pattern they form follows Fibonacci numbers.

plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Silvery, aromatic foliage rises into slender spikes of fragrant violet-blue blooms. Bees crowd the rows on warm afternoons. The scent drifts across hillsides and gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer, typically late June through August in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Provence in southern France, and gardens across temperate Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Lavender belongs to the mint family. Its name likely comes from the Latin word for washing, because the Romans scented their baths with it.

plants.name: Eucalyptus caesia
plants.description: A graceful, weeping tree with silvery-white bark and powdery blue-grey branches. Large, nectar-rich flowers hang in showy clusters. They draw honeyeaters and other birds through the cool season.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to winter, roughly May through September in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Granite outcrops of Western Australia's Wheatbelt
plants.funFact: Silver Princess Gum grows wild in only a few spots in Western Australia. It is a protected species there, yet it is popular in gardens around the world.
